extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys (practitioners in patent prosecution)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures for shortened statutory periods, specified time limits, and extensions of time in U.S. patent prosecution (under 35 U.S.C. and 37 CFR 1.136), including examples, consequences, and petition/fee mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum shortened statutory periods for specific items
rubrics_metrics.description: A shortened statutory period may not be less than (1) The period for submitting an oath or declaration in compliance with § 1.63; 30 days (35 U.S.C. 133). (2) The period for submitting formal drawings set under § 1.85(c); 1 MONTH (NOT LESS THAN 30 DAYS). (3) The period for making a deposit set under § 1.809(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These minimums govern shortened statutory periods unless changed under rare special circumstances. See MPEP § 710.02(e) and related statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to set shortened statutory periods (35 U.S.C. 133 / 37 CFR 1.136)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.136 (35 U.S.C. 133) an applicant may be required to reply in a shorter period than 6 months, not less than 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situations in which shortened periods are used are listed in MPEP § 710.02(b). Shortened statutory periods are subject to the provisions of 37 CFR 1.136(a) unless applicant is notified otherwise in an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence and formatting of shortened time for reply
rubrics_metrics.description: An indication of a shortened time for reply should appear prominently on the first page of all copies of actions in which a shortened time for reply has been set so that a person merely scanning the action can easily see it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time limit requirement should be typed in capital letters where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of standard shortened-period durations and situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Common shortened statutory periods and their typical uses: 1 MONTH: e.g., requirement for restriction/election of species only (no action on the merits); to correct an inadvertent omission in a bona fide nonfinal reply. 2 MONTHS: winning party in a terminated interference to reply to an unanswered Office action; reply to an Ex parte Quayle Office action (application in condition for allowance except formal matters). 3 MONTHS: to reply to any Office action on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: MPEP § 809.02(a), § 817, § 714.03, § 714.14, § 2173.05(n), and Chapter 2300 for interference contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restarting the period for reply when Office action contains a correctable defect
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the citation of a reference is incorrect or an Office action contains some other defect and this error is called to the attention of the Office within 1 month of the mail date of the action, the Office will restart the previously set period for reply to run from the date the error is corrected, if requested to do so by applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 710.06 for procedure to request restart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified time limits (distinct from shortened statutory periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain situations use specified time limits for taking an action where failure to timely take the specified action results in a consequence other than abandonment (e.g., 3 weeks to object to a petition for access under 37 CFR 1.14(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified time limits include (A) petition for access objections (usually 3 weeks); (B) completion of an IDS missing content (1 month) where failure places IDS in file but noncomplying information not considered; (C) canceling claims to nonelected inventions when an application is otherwise allowable (e.g., 1 month); (D) adding a suggested claim to provoke an interference (not less than 1 month). Failure to timely comply with a specified time limit normally does NOT cause abandonment but triggers the particular consequence (e.g., decision on petition, cancellation, concession of priority).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified time limits can be shorter than 30 days and are not shortened statutory periods
rubrics_metrics.description: A specified time or time limit is not a shortened statutory period under 35 U.S.C. 133; the Office may specify a time for taking action (or a time limit) of less than the 30 day minimum specified in 35 U.S.C. 133.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because these are not statutory periods, they may be set below 30 days and the Office may excuse short delays at the examiner's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences difference: specified time limit vs shortened statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: The penalty attaching to failure to take a particular action within a specified time is a loss of rights in regard to the particular matter (e.g., failure to timely copy suggested claims results in a disclaimer). A failure to reply within the set statutory period under 35 U.S.C. 133 results in abandonment of the entire application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandonment of an application is not appealable, but a petition to revive may be granted if delay was unavoidable (37 CFR 1.137(a)) or unintentional (37 CFR 1.137(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner discretion for excusing short delays in specified time limits but not in statutory periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant replies a day or two after the specified time, the delay may be excused by the examiner if satisfactorily explained. A reply 1 day late in an application carrying a shortened statutory period under 35 U.S.C. 133, no matter what the excuse, results in abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of shortened statutory periods may be obtained under 37 CFR 1.136, provided the extension does not go beyond the 6-month statutory period from the date of the Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a): petition and fee mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: (a)(1) If an applicant is required to reply within a nonstatutory or shortened statutory time period, applicant may extend the time period for reply up to the earlier of the expiration of any maximum period set by statute or five months after the time period set for reply, if a petition for an extension of time and the fee set in § 1.17(a) are filed, unless: (i) Applicant is notified otherwise in an Office action; (ii) The reply is a reply brief submitted pursuant to § 41.41; (iii) The reply is a request for an oral hearing submitted pursuant to § 41.47(a); (iv) The reply is to a decision by the Board pursuant to § 1.304 or to § 41.50 or § 41.52; or (v) The application is involved in a contested case 41.101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date on which the petition and the fee have been filed is the date for determining the period of extension and the corresponding amount of the fee. The expiration of the time period is determined by the amount of the fee paid. A reply must be filed prior to the expiration of the period of extension to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3) constructive petition and fee authorizations (safety net)
rubrics_metrics.description: A written request may be submitted that is an authorization to treat any concurrent or future reply requiring a petition for an extension of time under this paragraph as incorporating a petition for extension. An authorization to charge all required fees or submission of the fee will be treated as a constructive petition for an extension of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a 'safety net' to avoid loss of rights when a petition is inadvertently omitted. The Office strongly recommends including a written petition in reply to avoid processing delays. A short sample petition form paragraph is provided in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.136(b): extensions for sufficient cause when (a) unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reply cannot be filed within the time period set and the provisions of paragraph (a) are not available, the period for reply will be extended only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified. Any request must be filed on or before the day on which such reply is due and must be accompanied by the petition fee under § 1.17(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests will be decided by the Technology Center (TC) Director. The mere filing of the request does not effect an extension. No extension can operate to extend the time beyond the 6-month statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions where 37 CFR 1.136(a) extensions are not available
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not available for: (A) all extensions in a reexamination proceeding; (B) all extensions during an interference proceeding (but not preparatory to an interference where a claim is suggested); (C) situations where an Office action states that 1.136(a) is not applicable (e.g., reply to a notice of allowability, reissue applications associated with litigation, applications in allowable condition with nonelected claims set to cancel); and (D) limited instances where applicant is given a specified time limit to take certain actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2265, 2665, Chapter 2300 and relevant CFR provisions for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-extendable time periods in Notice of Allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant is notified in a 'Notice of Allowability' that an application is otherwise in condition for allowance, the following time periods are not extendable if set in the Notice or in an Office action having a mail date on or after the Notice: (1) The period for submitting an oath or declaration in compliance with § 1.63; (2) The period for submitting formal drawings set under § 1.85(c); (3) The period for making a deposit set under § 1.809(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) or (b) are NOT available to correct such informalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for extensions are cumulative; small-entity reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees for extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(a) and are subject to a 50% reduction for persons or concerns qualifying as small entities. The fees itemized at 37 CFR 1.17(a) are cumulative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if a 1-month extension fee (1.17(a)(1)) was paid and an additional 1 month is needed, the proper fee is the amount in 1.17(a)(2) less the amount previously paid (1.17(a)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of petition/fee filing determines extension period and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.136(a)(2) provides that the date on which the petition and the fee have been filed is the date for purposes of determining the period of extension and the corresponding amount of the fee. The expiration of the time period is determined by the amount of the fee paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply must be filed prior to the expiration of the period of extension to avoid abandonment; in no situation may an applicant reply later than the maximum statutory period set by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office practice treating under-sized petitions as requesting appropriate extension when fee authorization present
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition for an extension requests an insufficient period such that the petition would be filed outside the so-extended period, but the petition or application contains an authorization to charge extension fees to a deposit account, Office practice is to treat the petition as requesting the period of extension necessary to make the petition filed within the further extended period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a 2-month petition filed 4.5 months after notice of appeal may be treated as requesting a 3-month extension if there is fee authorization, so the petition is construed to the appropriate period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies filed after set period without petition/fee are not timely until petition and fee submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a reply is filed after the set period for reply has expired and no petition or fee accompanies it, the reply will not be accepted as timely until the petition (which may be a constructive petition under 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3)) and the appropriate fee are submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if Office action sets 3-month period and applicant replies in 4th month with a petition for a 1-month extension only, the reply is not acceptable until the fee is filed; if fee filed in 5th month, additional fee for second month required to render reply timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions not necessary for supplemental replies if initial reply timely filed
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136 is not necessary when submitting a supplemental reply to an Office action if a complete first reply was timely filed in reply to the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No petition/fee required in that context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neither primary examiner nor Director may extend shortened statutory period without petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the primary examiner nor the Director of the USPTO has authority to extend the shortened statutory period unless a petition for the extension is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the shortened period may be extended within limits of the statutory 6 months period, no extension can operate to extend time beyond the 6 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative handling of 37 CFR 1.136(b) duplicate requests with return envelope
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for extension under 37 CFR 1.136(b) is filed in duplicate and accompanied by a stamped return-addressed envelope, the Office will indicate the action taken on the duplicate and return it promptly in the envelope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation on original (part of file) should be signed by person granting/denying and the name/title should appear on the copy returned; when granted/denied, extent or reason indicated on originals and returned copy. Optional procedure; IFW processing considerations apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required final-rejection wording when setting 3-month shortened statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: For a final rejection setting a 3-month shortened statutory period, the examiner must include the following language in each final rejection: 'A SHORTENED STATUTORY PERIOD FOR REPLY TO THIS FINAL ACTION IS SET TO EXPIRE THREE MONTHS FROM THE DATE OF THIS ACTION. IN THE EVENT A FIRST REPLY IS FILED WITHIN TWO MONTHS ... THEN THE SHORTENED STATUTORY PERIOD WILL EXPIRE ON THE DATE THE ADVISORY ACTION IS MAILED, AND ANY EXTENSION FEE ... WILL BE CALCULATED FROM THE MAILING DATE OF THE ADVISORY ACTION. IN NO EVENT WILL THE STATUTORY PERIOD FOR REPLY EXPIRE LATER THAN SIX MONTHS FROM THE DATE OF THIS FINAL ACTION.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This language governs computation of due dates when an advisory action is involved and caps statutory period at six months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time for affidavits after final rejection: limited effect and admissibility
rubrics_metrics.description: When requests for extension of time are filed after final rejection to permit submission of an affidavit, granting the extension is without prejudice to the examiner's right to question why the affidavit was not earlier presented. If applicant's showing is insufficient, the examiner may deny entry of the affidavit notwithstanding grant of the extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission or refusal of such an affidavit does not save the application from abandonment; affidavits submitted after final rejection are subject to the same treatment as amendments submitted after final rejection (see 37 CFR 1.116(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: No extensions of time after payment of issue fee (nonextendable issue-fee period)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory (nonextendable) time period for payment of the issue fee is 3 months from the date of the Notice of Allowance (35 U.S.C. 151).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informalities outstanding at time of allowance (drawing corrections, supplemental declarations, etc.) must be corrected and fees paid within the 3-month period; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) or (b) are NOT available to correct such informalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two periods running: earlier statutory period not suspended by later specified time action
rubrics_metrics.description: When two different periods for reply are running against an application (one limited by the regular statutory period, the other by a limited period set in a subsequent Office action), the running of the first period is not suspended nor affected by an ex parte limited time action or even by an appeal therefrom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example (copying patent claims): where claims copied from a patent are rejected and other claims have an unanswered rejection, the controlling date of the statutory period is the date of the last unanswered Office action on the non-copied claims. See Ex parte Milton and Chapter 2300 for interference related exceptions.
